messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: nichemapR in unix
parts:
Hi Simon,

Not in the near future at this stage I'm afraid. Unfortunately I am unable to provide the source Fortran code which is the reason you can't compile it yourself. I looked into whether one can include UNIX pre-compiled libraries in an R package along with Windows and OSX and hit a dead end. If you know a way round that, let me know. Hopefully in the not-too-distant-future the source Fortran can be released as part of the package.

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 9c7ab3c81d833137
messages.subject: Re: nichemapR in unix
parts:
Hi Mike,

Many thanks for the response - I thought that may be the case! I've been looking to see whether it's possible to 'emulate' Windows/OSX packages within a Linux environment but have also hit a dead end. 

I've been attempting to run the micro climate model across a large swathe of central and south America so have been prepping everything to run across a UNIX cluster to speed things up. I did initially try to run the code for the micro_climate() function on its own (without requiring the whole NicheMapR package to be installed) but it  needs the .dllc so I get a bunch of errors when I attempt this. I'll look into this some more to see if there's a hacky solution, even if it's at the expense of some decrease in speed. If not, I'll chunk up my geographical extent and get it running across several PCs instead.

Many thanks,
Simon
